result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_assortativity_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate degree assortativity coefficient. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29056-L29135){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_assortativity_degree() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Degree assortativity](/assets/graphs/get-assortativity-degree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two hubs C and D, each with degree 3, linked to each other and to two leaves of degree 1 apiece. Four of the five edges join a high-degree node to a low-degree one (accent), so mixing is disassortative and r = -0.667." width="100%"} Measures the tendency of nodes to connect to other nodes with similar degrees. Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of node degrees across edges, quantifying whether high-degree nodes preferentially connect to other high-degree nodes (assortative) or to low-degree nodes (disassortative). For directed graphs, uses out-degree for source nodes and in-degree for target nodes. For undirected graphs, uses total degree. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Assortativity coefficient in range [-1, 1]: - r > 0: assortative mixing (similar degrees connect) - r < 0: disassortative mixing (different degrees connect) - r ≈ 0: no degree correlation ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph has no edges or insufficient degree variance. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Assortativity by degree (Newman, 2002) is the Pearson correlation between the degrees of edge endpoints, evaluated across every edge in the graph: $r = \dfrac{\sum_{xy} xy\,(e_{xy} - a_x b_y)}{\sigma_a \sigma_b}$, where $e_{xy}$ is the observed joint distribution of endpoint-degree pairs and $a_x, b_y$ are its marginals. On directed graphs the natural convention pairs each edge's *source out-degree* with its *target in-degree*; undirected graphs use total degree symmetrically. Real-world social networks tend toward $r > 0$ (hubs connect to hubs, a signature of homophilic wiring), while technological and biological networks (power grids, protein-interaction networks, the Web) are consistently disassortative ($r < 0$). ## Examples {.doc-examples} When high-degree "influencer" nodes mostly connect to each other, while low-degree nodes connect among themselves, the degree assortativity comes out positive: ::: {#4df1cc0e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for label in ["Influencer1", "Influencer2", "Influencer3", "User1", "User2", "User3", "User4"]: g.add_node(label=label) g.add_edge(source="Influencer1", target="Influencer2") g.add_edge(source="Influencer1", target="Influencer3") g.add_edge(source="Influencer2", target="Influencer3") g.add_edge(source="User1", target="User2") g.add_edge(source="User3", target="User4") # Returns a positive value: hubs connect to hubs, periphery to periphery g.get_assortativity_degree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: A client-server topology is the opposite case: a few high-degree servers connect to many low-degree clients, which gives a negative (disassortative) coefficient: ::: {#b79f59a6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for label in ["Server1", "Server2", "Client1", "Client2", "Client3", "Client4", "Client5"]: g.add_node(label=label) g.add_edge(source="Server1", target="Client1") g.add_edge(source="Server1", target="Client2") g.add_edge(source="Server1", target="Client3") g.add_edge(source="Server2", target="Client4") g.add_edge(source="Server2", target="Client5") # Returns a negative value: high-degree nodes connect to low-degree nodes g.get_assortativity_degree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` -0.8421052631578951 ``` ::: :::
